claims.text: Randomly distributed multiple principal elements produce severe lattice distortion in high-entropy alloys.
Severe lattice distortion creates a heterogeneous dislocation landscape.
The heterogeneous dislocation landscape slows and diversifies dislocation motion during dynamic loading.
Sluggish dislocation mobility enables simultaneous activation of multiple slip systems and/or twinning.
Delayed dislocation motion and enhanced work hardening produce high strength, while distributed plasticity maintains high ductility.
The proposed initial material is a chemically disordered, single-phase BCC or FCC high-entropy alloy.
The proposed initial material has significant atomic-size mismatch.
The controlled comparison should test a high-distortion HEA against a lower-distortion conventional alloy with matched phase and similar microstructure.
Testing should use room or moderately elevated temperatures and strain rates high enough to reveal dynamic dislocation activity without thermal softening.
Local lattice-strain heterogeneity modifies dislocation-core structures.
Local lattice-strain heterogeneity promotes both dislocation glide and twinning.
Severe lattice distortion raises energy barriers for conventional dislocation glide.
Slower glide forces distributed activation of additional slip systems and twinning under dynamic loading.
Relative to the conventional-alloy baseline, the HEA will have higher yield strength.
Relative to the conventional-alloy baseline, the HEA will have comparable or greater total elongation.
The HEA will exhibit a more heterogeneous dislocation structure and evidence of multiple active slip systems, with possible localized twinning.
The lower-distortion conventional baseline is expected to have less dispersed dislocation activity and lower strain-hardening capacity during dynamic loading.
The mechanism should apply to both single-phase FCC and BCC HEAs having significant lattice distortion.
The mechanism may cease to apply in multiphase HEAs or at extremely high temperatures where thermally activated recovery dominates.
A failure to observe the predicted mechanical-property advantage or any difference in dislocation heterogeneity and deformation modes would falsify the hypothesis.
